shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: White avens: herbaceous perennial with many-part compound BASAL LEAVES (large terminal leaflet), smaller often 3-part CAULINE leaves, white five-petaled flowers and an aggregate burr of ACHENES with hooked persistent lower STYLE segments. Examine achenes close-up; green 'burr' is the highest-value family/genus structure.
shared_genus_recognition.identity_warning: Source-pool reference only, exact-species full scientific review and range status handled separately

genus_comparison_matrix.source_taxon: Slender erect branching woodland herb typically ~30–100 cm, leafy stems and basal rosette
genus_comparison_matrix.reference_contrast: Not a sprawling Rubus prickly woody cane; Potentilla usually different habit.

genus_comparison_matrix.source_taxon: Basal leaves simple or pinnate, terminal leaflet clearly larger; upper leaves 3-foliolate or 3-lobed
genus_comparison_matrix.reference_contrast: Different leaf architectures on same plant prevent mis-ID if one leaf is isolated.

genus_comparison_matrix.source_taxon: White 5-petal star with many free stamens and separate pistils in a green hypanthium
genus_comparison_matrix.reference_contrast: Other Rosaceae/Fragaria/Potentilla can have similar 5-petaled flowers; need fruit.

genus_comparison_matrix.source_taxon: Round head of numerous separate dry achenes, not juicy drupelets
genus_comparison_matrix.reference_contrast: Rubus forms many fleshy drupelets; Geum forms hooked dry achenes.

genus_comparison_matrix.source_taxon: Each achene retains a lower jointed persistent style ending in curved HOOK, distal part sheds
genus_comparison_matrix.reference_contrast: Hooked style is especially useful for G. canadense; not all Geum species have equal hooks.

genus_comparison_matrix.source_taxon: Receptacle/torus densely bristly in fruit; pedicel often hairy, sepals reflex
genus_comparison_matrix.reference_contrast: Use a precise mature fruit macro, not a fuzzy silhouette.

look_here_first_sequence: Recognize plant architecture and leaf arrangement before flower color.
Compare leaf shape, insertion and microstructures on several mature samples.
Inspect floral anatomy under magnification and track into mature fruit.
Cross-check the strongest lookalike with matched scale; avoid uncertain species IDs.
Respect the source-name/canonical manifest boundary and keep nonlocal native labels unchanged.
scientific_cautions: Geum canadense is pool-only/uninstalled; this module is not a species install or county native proof.
FNA notes variant/possible southwestern forms including some Texas early-spring plants; do not invent a separate subspecies/variety.
Hooked styles are a species-level feature but not universal throughout large Geum genus; no false 'all avens have burr hooks'.
Do not use an image labeled Geum laciniatum as a substitute for G. canadense; exact-species image checking required.

handoffs.task: Photo polish must verify exact-species mature hooked style macro with rights, not rely on generic avens/Geum laciniatum stock. Installer lane to handle approved source-pool status separately.
Acquire the six exact diagnostic panels, tagged photographer/license/source and permit private-study-only only where rights say so.
